sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Deventer's parking policy is being rewritten, and the documents we found are drafts. A consultation draft of a new Nota parkeerbeleid, whose PDF was last modified on 23 April 2026, would withdraw the 2013 parking policy plan and the 2015 rules; we found no source showing that the council has adopted it [0]. The draft makes paid parking the main steering tool, uses no blue zones, keeps street parking pricier than garages and aims not to add street spaces in the centre, with at most one resident permit per address [1]. It would also let the college propose new or extended paid zones in the centre and surrounding districts without the current requirement of over 50 percent resident support per street, triggered by peak pressure above 85 percent [2]. Meanwhile surveys and requests to introduce parking regulation are paused while the parking products are renewed [3]. A consultation poster from April 2026 defines an 'autoluwe' centre as mainly for pedestrians, cyclists and public transport, with cars allowed where needed [4].

Current rules: the parking tax ordinance, adopted on 12 November 2025 and applying from 1 January 2026, sets street parking at 3.53 euros an hour in inner-city zones 1 and 2 with a 25 euro day card, and 3.00 euros on the Singels [5]. Residents' street permits cost 362 euros a year in the inner city [11]. On 21 April 2026 the college proposed a 3.2 percent increase in parking tariffs, permits and subscriptions for 2027, a proposal not yet decided [12]. A scan car has checked street parking payment since 1 June 2026 as a trial of 1.5 years [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The council's 2026 mobility programme expects the Stationsplein garage to lose its public function over time because of the Topicus masterplan, and the Verzetslaan car park, with land bought in 2025, to become a park once a temporary mobility hub near the NS park-and-ride exists; hub De Kien is expected to open in 2028, followed by one at Roto Smeets, with no closing dates stated [14]. The Brinkgarage shares a grid connection with a pumping station and cannot get a larger one, and pump work in 2027 may affect its capacity [15]. Charge points in the centre are in five garages, and a request for a new public charge point must be outside the inner city; the city invited comments on 11 candidate locations from 8 June to 17 July [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipal garages Brink, Stadspoort and Stationsplein, managed by P1, charge 1 euro per 27 minutes by day Monday to Saturday, with a 10 euro daily maximum, and the city says garage parking in the centre is cheaper than street parking [6]. Subscriptions cost 794 euros a year for residents, and all municipal garages have waiting lists [10]. Garage parking income was 1.76 million euros in 2025, up from 1.52 million in 2024, out of total parking income of 7.16 million euros [13]. Five large contracts, including garage equipment and the agreement with the parking manager, expire in 2027 with tendering to start in 2026 [7]. The Centrumgarage (Op de Keizer, 575 spaces) was founded in 1978 by city-centre retailers and charges up to 12 euros a day [8]. Q-Park runs De Boreel (604 spaces) and P+R Handelskade (247) [9].

Our data cover two of these: the Centrumgarage and P+R Handelskade, 822 spaces, measured for 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 44% on weekdays and 43% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Centrumgarage averaged 44% and 45%, and P+R Handelskade 45% on weekdays and 37% at weekends; both reached full in single readings. We have no readings for the three municipal garages. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
